crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Clause Extraction and Obligation Analysis
children.blurb: Clause extraction and obligation analysis is the part of contract work that finds specific provisions in an agreement and works out what each party must do, when, and under what conditions.

children.name: Agent Redlining and Negotiation
children.blurb: Agent redlining and negotiation covers software agents that read a draft contract, compare it to a playbook or prior positions, propose edits, and exchange revised language with a counterparty or another agent.

children.name: Smart Contracts and Executable Terms
children.blurb: Smart contracts and executable terms are agreements whose performance is carried out by software rather than by human action alone.

children.name: Obligation and Service Level Tracking
children.blurb: Obligation and service level tracking is the practice of identifying, recording, and monitoring the promises and performance targets that a contract creates.

children.name: Generative Template Drafting
children.blurb: Generative template drafting is the use of generative AI models to produce contract templates, clause libraries, and first drafts of agreements from structured inputs.

sections.body: Contract lifecycle and algorithmic drafting is the use of AI to read, write, negotiate, and monitor agreements across their life from template to signature to renewal. In practice, AI systems extract clauses and defined terms from long documents, compare them against playbooks, and flag deviations for human review. Agent redlining tools propose edits, accept or reject changes, and sometimes negotiate with another agent under limits set by a person. Executable contracts turn some terms into code that can trigger payments or access rights automatically. Obligation tracking watches deadlines, service levels, and renewal notices after signing. Generative template drafting produces first drafts from a deal description and a firm's prior language.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is uneven. Clause extraction is mature for common contract types and clean digital text, but it still struggles with scanned exhibits, unusual formatting, and cross references that change meaning. Redlining agents can save time on routine terms, yet they do not understand business context, relationship history, or the risk of an ambiguous concession. Smart contracts are real but narrow, because most agreements depend on judgment, changing facts, and dispute resolution that code cannot fully capture. Obligation tracking is only as good as the data feeding it, and missed notices remain a common failure. The honest limits are liability, confidentiality, privilege, and the need for a human to own the final call, and the site tracks 220 compliance and regulation pages, which reflects how often contract terms must answer to external rules that shift by jurisdiction.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages under this section follow the contract from intake to performance. Clause Extraction and Obligation Analysis is the entry point for pulling structure and duties out of existing documents. Agent Redlining and Negotiation covers the back and forth of edits, including how AI agents propose changes and where human approval stops them. Smart Contracts and Executable Terms explains when code can carry out a term and when it cannot. Obligation and Service Level Tracking follows the signed deal, watching dates, metrics, and remedies. Generative Template Drafting shows how first drafts are assembled from prior language and deal facts, and a reader would start with extraction to understand inputs, move to redlining and drafting for creation, then use tracking and executable terms for what happens after signature.
